title: Venom profiling of the insular species Bothrops alcatraz: characterization of proteome, glycoproteome, and N-terminome using Terminal Amine Isotopic Labeling of Substrates.
projectDescription: In this study we applied mass spectrometric approaches to characterize the proteome and glycoproteome of B. alcatraz venom, and to show for the first time the use of the TAILS method to profile a snake venom N-terminome.
sampleProcessingProtocol: • Proteomic analysis of snake venom: venom samples were submitted to protein quantification by the Bradford assay and submitted to trypsin digestion. The protocol used guanidine hydrochloride for protein denaturation step and dithiothreitol (DTT) for disulfide bonds reduction and iodoacetamide (IAA) for carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues. • Glycoproteomic analysis of B. alcatraz venom: Glycoprotein enrichment was performed by lectin-affinity chromatography using three different resins: Concanavalin A-Sepharose (ConA), Wheat Germ Agglutinin-agarose (WGA) and Peanut Agglutinin-agarose (PNA). For glycoprotein elution, we used carbohydrate solutions, according to each lectin specificity. A second round of elution was performed using an acidic solution to elute the retained proteins. The bound fractions were cleaned up and submitted to trypsin digestion using guanidine hydrochloride as denaturing agent.  • N-terminomic analysis of B. alcatraz venom: For the analysis of the protein N-terminal sequences, the first steps involved denaturation of venom proteins by guanidine hydrochloride, reduction by DTT and carbamidomethylation using IAA. After these steps, the proteins were submitted to a dimethylation reaction using formaldehyde and sodium cyanoborohydride. Then, the proteins were cleaved by trypsin to generate peptides for LC-MS/MS. To perform the depletion of the tryptic peptides, the samples were applied to an aldehyde-activated crosslinked 4% beaded agarose resin and the natural N-terminal peptides were collected from the flow through fraction since they did not bind to the resin due their dimethylated N-termini. • Peptide desalting and fractionation: Peptide samples were desalted and/or fractionated by stage tip with the membrane set C18-SCX-C18. • LC-MS/MS: All LC-MS/MS analyses were performed in an EASY II-nanoLC system coupled to an LTQ-Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Samples were injected in a 3 cm C18 trap column (100 μm I.D. × 360 μm O.D.) and the chromatographic peptide separations were performed on 10 cm long columns (75 μm I.D. x 360 μm O.D.) packed in-house with 5 μm Aqua C-18 beads (Phenomenex).
dataProcessingProtocol: All data analyses were performed using MaxQuant (version 1.6.10.43) and Perseus (version 1.6.10.45).
keywords: Bothrops alcatraz; snake venom; proteome; glycoproteome; n-terminome; proteolytic processing
